Title: Secretary stresses need for obtaining maximum benefit from AKU-CEL's diploma programme
NewsSummary: Additional Secretary Education, Government of Sindh, Mr Deedar Murtaza has asked for increasing the number of fellowships offered by Higher Education Commission for the Advanced Diploma conducted by Aga Khan University Centre of English Language (AKU
NewsContent:
Additional Secretary Education, Government of Sindh, Mr Deedar Murtaza has asked for increasing the number of fellowships offered by Higher Education Commission for the Advanced Diploma conducted by Aga Khan University Centre of English Language (AKU-CEL) in Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL). He was speaking at the first diploma award ceremony of Advanced Diploma Programme in TEFL at AKU-CEL.

Appreciating the quality of training at AKU-CEL, he said, "Looking at the dire need for training in the public sector, the number of these fellowships should be increased so that maximum benefit can be obtained from the endeavours made by AKU-CEL."

Mr Murtaza, who was the chief guest at the occasion, also lamented the poor standard of English language teaching in Pakistan which has made access to higher education a wistful dream for many. He expressed the need to train English language teachers, especially from the public sector, in the latest ELT approaches and methodologies to ensure quality teaching.

Advanced Diploma Programme in TEFL is offered at AKU-CEL through higher education links with the University of Warwick, UK and with the support of the British Council. HEC has also supported the programme by offering fifteen fellowships to teachers working in public sector universities and colleges. ADP in TEFL aims to improve the standard of English language teaching in higher education in Pakistan by strengthening teachers through professional development.

Earlier, in his welcome speech, AKU President Shamsh Kassim-Lakha, H.I., S. I., stressed the importance of English in higher education and said, "The role of English for access to higher education is undeniable." He also congratulated the faculty of AKU-CEL for having established their credibility as an academic unit of the University as well as making meaningful contributions to the field of English language teaching in the country.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr Mohammad Khurshid, Dean Medical College, AKU shared the details of the programme with the audience and congratulated AKU-CEL on its success.

Dr Sabiha Mansoor, Head, AKU-CEL in her closing remarks thanked the guests and reiterated CEL's commitment to play its role in the development of English language teaching in higher education in Pakistan.

The quality of its educational initiatives has made AKU a role model for other institutions in the region. When reviewing existing programmes or adding new ones, AKU ensures the attributes of quality, relevance and impact are kept in mind.

"A graduating student receives the diploma from Mr Deedar Murtaza, Additional Secretary Education, Government of Sindh, at the Aga Khan University Centre of English Language's award Ceremony for its Advanced Diploma Programme. Acting Provost Dr. David Taylor stands in the middle."
